title: Micro rollback protocol and checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a light-weight, personal-first runbook for performing small, urgent rollbacks and targeted mitigations after a bad merge. Focus is on changes that touch serving runtime, routing, or rollout configs where a full incident runbook is overkill but we still need a repeatable, low-risk path to restore steady state.

Scope & when to use:
- Use for single-PR regressions or config flips that increase error rate, latency, or bring down a small fraction of traffic.
- Not for major outages that require pager/SRE incident response (use full incident runbook).
- Prefer when: regression introduced in last 2 deploys; can be reverted without DB migrations or broad schema changes.

Quick decision checklist (5 items):
1) Does revert remove the unsafe change? (yes -> proceed)
2) Are there active canaries/rollouts targeting the change? (identify, pause)
3) Is the change tied to migrations or external side effects? (if yes -> escalate)
4) Can we validate rollback within 10 minutes with smoke checks? (if yes -> proceed)
5) Who is the rollback owner and communicator? (declare one person)

Pre-rollback steps (owner must confirm):
- Identify failing PR/commit hash and the deploy that introduced it.
- Check rollout plan: canary percentage, target hosts, route rules.
- Post a short message in #eng-runtime (or incident channel) with summary and plan.
- Grab quick logs & traces for a representative failing request (top 3 errors).
- If a dedicated model or GPU pool is involved, note capacity/queue impact.

Rollback variants (pick one):
A) Revert the PR and re-deploy (preferred when CI + infra quick):
  - Create revert PR referencing original (use GitHub UI or CLI).
  - Run minimal CI (unit + smoke); mark with rollback tag.
  - Merge and deploy to the same pipeline as original.
B) Hotfix patch (small code change to undo behavior):
  - Submit small targeted PR that flips behavior flag or adds guard.
  - Test locally or via canary, then push.
C) Routing/feature flag flip (fastest, safest):
  - If feature flag exists, flip it off for affected scope.
  - If rollout config is in system, reduce percentage to 0 or route away.
D) Infrastructure fallback (model variant swap):
  - Route to a previous model variant or smaller capacity pool while investigating.

Commands & snippets (examples, adjust to repo):
- Find deploy: git log --grep="<PR#>" --oneline --max-count=1
- Create revert: gh pr create --body "revert of #<PR>" --title "revert: <short>"
- Re-deploy pipeline: ./scripts/deploy.sh --pipeline runtime-stable --commit <sha>
- Flip flag (console): curl -XPOST -H "Auth: $TOKEN" https://config.redwood/api/flags/feature-x/disable

Validation checklist (post-rollback):
- Smoke: endpoint /health returns ok on 10 hosts (5 region samples).
- Latency: 95th p90 returns to baseline within 2x window (watch dashboard).
- Error rate: relevant SLI falls back to baseline or acceptable threshold within 10 minutes.
- Trace sanity: no new big spikes in tail latencies in traces.
- End-user sampling: run 3 manual flows that previously failed.

Monitoring dashboards to watch (quick set):
- runtime/latency-by-route (p50/p95/p99)
- runtime/error-rate-by-code (5min)
- rollout/traffic-distribution (by region & model)
- infra/gpu-queue-depth (if model swap)
- logging/exception-sample (grep for original error strings)

Communication template (post in channel & thread):
- Subject: quick rollback executed for PR #<PR> — reverted commit <sha>
- Summary: Reverted PR which caused elevated 500s for route /v1/generate under high prompt-length.
- Impact: ~3% of requests affected, latency up ~1.2s for 90th.
- Action: Reverted & re-deployed at 15:42 UTC; monitoring shows error rate back to baseline.
- Owner: Ishani Patel (followups invited)

Post-rollback followups (owner tasks):
- Create a short postmortem stub in the incident page (1–2 paragraphs + timeline).
- Add automated smoke test that reproduces failure pattern to PR gating.
- If rollback was routing/flag, schedule a follow-up PR that addresses root cause.
- Tag original author for context and pair on fix if needed.

Mini checklist for reviewers to reduce need for rollback (pre-merge heuristics):
- Does PR change routing/rollout config? If yes, require a staged rollout plan.
- Does latency-sensitive path change kernel or model selection? Add perf baseline in CI.
- If touching cache (KV/prefix) ensure TTLs and key formats are backward compatible.
- Any changes that flip feature flags should include an automated flag toggle test in CI.
- Add explicit observability: new counters / tags, delta dashboards.

Notes / heuristics I've collected while doing small rollbacks:
- Reverting the PR is cleaner than patching in many cases — reduces long tail of tech debt.
- Flipping flags is fastest but can mask root cause; only use as stopgap with a follow-up ticket.
- Keep the rollback PR title explicit: "revert: <original PR> — reason: brief" so it surfaces in search.
- When in doubt about DB or migrations, pause and escalate to SRE/DB owner — do not rollback blind.

Open questions / TODOs (for next iteration):
- Standardize a single curl-based flag toggle helper for engineers (small CLI).
- Add a rollback button in the console for simple route-only rollbacks (guarded by 2FA).
- Draft a tiny CI job template that runs a 1-min perf smoke for serving changes.

Quick references:
- Example revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/2198
- Incident page template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Incident+Template
- Jira for rollout work: INF-4821

Personal notes: Keep this doc minimal and copyable into a channel message. The goal is to move fast but cleanly: one owner, one action, confirm. If rollback triggers more than 3 cascading fixes, escalate to full postmortem.

-----
Changelog (local):
- 2025-01-14 created initial checklist
- 2025-03-02 added command snippets and validation steps
- 2026-02-28 expanded monitoring list and added TODOs for console helper
